title: Senior's toolkit: parallel, remote and secret
summary: The commands for fanning work out across threads and machines, and for handling the credentials that go with it.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: parallel, remote and secret
steps.body: Scale-out commands are where small mistakes get multiplied by the number of threads or servers. These are the tools, and the switches that keep them safe.

toolkit.what: Run a script block for many items at once (PowerShell 7).
flags: run the whole thing as a background job

toolkit.what: Background work in the same process, collected later.
flags: wait, collect and clean up in one go

toolkit.what: Run a script block on remote machines; results come back with PSComputerName.
toolkit.example: Invoke-Command -ComputerName (Get-Content servers.txt) { Get-Service W3SVC } | Where-Object Status -ne Running

toolkit.what: Keep connections open; or an interactive remote prompt.
toolkit.example:
$s = New-PSSession -HostName web01, web02 -UserName deploy
Invoke-Command -Session $s { Get-Date }

toolkit.what: Read and store secrets through SecretManagement, whatever the vault.
flags: only when an API needs a string
toolkit.example: $cred = Get-Secret -Name SqlAdmin    # a PSCredential stored with Set-Secret

toolkit.what: Plug a vault extension in behind SecretManagement.
Ask a human for a user name and password as a PSCredential.
toolkit.example: Set-Secret -Name SqlAdmin -Secret (Get-Credential -UserName sa -Message 'SQL admin for reports')

pairs: Ping 300 servers quickly from your machine
Start a long export and keep working
A password for a scheduled job
Pass the -Days value into a remote block

steps.prompt: `Invoke-Command -ComputerName $servers { Get-Process } | ForEach-Object { $_.Kill() }` fails on every object. Why?
options: The returned objects are deserialised snapshots without methods; stop the processes inside the script block
ForEach-Object does not accept remote objects
steps.explain: Results come back as `Deserialized.System.Diagnostics.Process`: properties only. Do the action where the object lives: `Invoke-Command -ComputerName $servers { Get-Process notepad | Stop-Process -WhatIf }`.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Pick a throttle for the system on the other end, not for your laptop. Pass every outside value into remote and parallel blocks with `$using:`, and put `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest` inside those blocks. Act remotely, bring back small results. Secrets come from a vault or the pipeline, never from the script.
